headline: High risk of capability conflict and cascading error from shared file-based workflows; prompt-injection and leakage are lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a content-writing repo with no declared shared channel, while agent B explicitly uses shared skill files and context-building. That makes direct injection from A into B unlikely by default, but if A’s text is copied into B’s files or prompts, B could follow it as instructions. The pathway is interaction-based, not inherent.
conditions: IF operator copies A-generated text into B skill files or prompts, injection becomes plausible.
IF B parses copied content as instructions without provenance checks, malicious instructions can steer behavior.
mitigations: Keep A outputs out of B skill files.
Add a one-line provenance header before any copied text.
Review copied content before B consumes it.
Use separate folders for A and B artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to B's file ingestion.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no declared data classes and has no I/O surfaces, while B reads and writes files and calls APIs. There is no documented shared workspace or sensitive data class overlap, so leakage is not established. If the operator places confidential material into B’s workspace and then reuses it in A prompts, leakage can occur through copied content rather than a built-in channel.
conditions: IF the same workspace contains confidential files for B and those files are later pasted into A prompts, leakage is possible.
IF B uploads copied file contents to its APIs, those contents leave the local environment.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in B's working directory.
Use a redacted copy for any A/B handoff.
Audit B API calls before running.
Separate local and networked workspaces.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and DLP scanning.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no declared write or network capabilities, but B can read and write the filesystem, spawn subprocesses, and use allowlisted network egress. B also supports multiple instances and shared-context skills, so concurrent writes or state drift are plausible if both agents operate on the same files. A cannot be assumed to coordinate or lock, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF A and B are pointed at the same directory, concurrent edits can collide.
IF B runs multiple instances against shared files, last-write-wins corruption can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate directories to A and B.
Run only one B instance per workspace.
Use file locks for shared artifacts.
Check git status before and after each run.
requires-engineering: add transactional writes or locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B’s sandboxing says skills reference each other and build on shared context, so B may treat upstream outputs as authoritative. A is a content-writing agent, so its text can become B’s input and then be reused without verification. That creates a default pathway for compounding errors, though not necessarily irreversible harm.
conditions: IF A-generated text is fed into B's shared context, B may propagate mistakes.
IF B uses A output without a verification step, errors can cascade into downstream marketing assets.
mitigations: Require a human review step between A and B.
Mark A output as untrusted input.
Add a checklist for factual claims.
Compare B output against source material.
requires-engineering: add automated citation/claim verification.

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source content-writing repo with no declared data classes, while B handles marketing content and product marketing context. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to ordinary handling of marketing materials. Because only B has relevant data-handling fields, A is cited only to show the absence of a sensitive compliance surface.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is introduced into B's marketing workspace, compliance review becomes necessary.
IF B's file retention differs from the operator's policy, retention mismatch can arise.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B's workspace.
Document retention for marketing files.
Delete stale drafts after use.
Use a separate folder for regulated material.
requires-engineering: map data classes to retention and residency controls.
